implementation_notes: Vapor names the pattern directly: a type conforming to Authenticator - or AsyncBasicAuthenticator / AsyncBearerAuthenticator for the built-in credential shapes - inspects the request and calls req.auth.login(user) on success; the authenticator is attached with app.grouped(MyAuthenticator()) and protected code reads the typed principal via req.auth.require(User.self). Authenticators compose by grouping, and guardMiddleware enforces that one of them succeeded. CryptoKit and the Keychain API supply the primitives for custom mechanisms; the classic abstract-hierarchy is not written by hand.
pitfalls: Throwing on invalid credentials turns a 401 into a 500; return without logging in and let guardMiddleware reject the request.
req.auth is per-request storage; caching a user on the authenticator type is a cross-request identity leak.
An authenticator alone only attempts verification - without guardMiddleware a route can run unauthenticated.
Token verification must check signature, issuer, audience and expiry; JWTKit exposes the steps separately and does not apply them all by default.
